						RRB ALP Recruitment CEN 01/2025 Recruitment 2026: Apply for 9970 Vacancies (CEN No. 01/2025)

						
						The Indian Railways has officially announced the RRB ALP Recruitment 2025 under CEN No. 01/2025, opening up an incredible opportunity for job seekers across the country. With 9,970 Assistant Loco Pilot (ALP) vacancies available, this is one of the biggest railway recruitments of the year. If you've been waiting for a stable, government job with growth and benefits, now’s the time to act.

						The online application process begins on 12 April 2025 and the last date to register and pay the fee is 19 May 2025. Candidates aged between 18 to 30 years (for General category) are eligible to apply, with age relaxation provided for OBC (33 years) and SC/ST (35 years) categories as per government norms Candidates from different educational backgrounds, especially those with ITI, diploma, or engineering qualifications, are eligible to apply. Selection will be through CBT (Computer-Based Test), followed by an aptitude test and document verification.

						What makes this recruitment exciting is not just the number of posts, but the attractive salary, career progression, and the prestige of working with Indian Railways. Assistant Loco Pilots play a vital role in train operations, and the job offers both technical challenge and long-term security.

						To apply, candidates must visit the official website of their respective RRB zone (like RRB Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, etc.), complete the registration, upload necessary documents, and pay the application fee online.

						With competition expected to be high, it's important to apply early, prepare well, and keep checking the official websites for updates. Whether you're a fresher or looking for a government switch, RRB ALP 2025 is your chance to drive your career forward — quite literally!

						

						
						RRB ALP (CEN 01/2025) Exam Pattern and Syllabus

						Exam Pattern

						The recruitment process for the Assistant Loco Pilot (ALP) under Centralized Employment Notice (CEN) No. 01/2025 consists of the following stages:

						
							First Stage Computer Based Test (CBT-1)
							Second Stage Computer Based Test (CBT-2)
							Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT)
							Document Verification (DV)
							Medical Examination (ME)
						

						1. First Stage CBT (CBT-1)

						
							Purpose: Preliminary screening.
							Mode: Computer Based Test (CBT).
							Duration: 60 minutes (80 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe).
							Total Questions: 75 (Multiple Choice Questions).
							Total Marks: 75.
							Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
							Qualifying Marks:
							
								UR & EWS: 40%
								OBC (NCL): 30%
								SC: 30%
								ST: 25%
								2% relaxation for PwBD candidates in respective categories.
							
							
							Shortlisting: Candidates are shortlisted for CBT-2 at 15 times the number of vacancies per RRB (subject to variation). Marks are normalized for multi-shift exams.
						

						2. Second Stage CBT (CBT-2)

						
							Purpose: Detailed assessment of technical and general knowledge.
							Mode: Computer Based Test.
							Structure: Divided into two parts:
							
								Part A:
								
									Duration: 90 minutes (120 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe).
									Total Questions: 100.
									Total Marks: 100.
									Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
									Qualifying Marks:
									
										UR & EWS: 40%
										OBC (NCL): 30%
										SC: 30%
										ST: 25%
										2% relaxation for PwBD candidates.
									
									
								
								
								Part B:
								
									Purpose: Assess technical knowledge relevant to ALP.
									Duration: 60 minutes (80 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe).
									Total Questions: 75.
									Total Marks: 75.
									Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
									Qualifying Marks: 35% (no relaxation for any category).
								
								
							
							
							Shortlisting: Candidates qualifying in both Part A and Part B are eligible for CBAT.
						

						3. Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT)

						
							Purpose: Evaluate aptitude for safety-critical ALP role.
							Mode: Computer Based Test.
							Languages: English and Hindi only.
							Structure: Multiple test batteries assessing cognitive and psychomotor skills.
							Negative Marking: None.
							Qualifying Marks: Minimum 42 marks in each test battery (applicable to all candidates, no relaxation).
							Weightage:
							
								CBAT: 70%
								CBT-2 (Part A): 30% for final merit list.
							
							
							Shortlisting: Candidates are shortlisted for Document Verification based on combined performance.
						

						4. Document Verification (DV)

						
							Purpose: Verify eligibility through original documents.
							Requirements:
							
								Original certificates (educational, technical, caste, age, etc.) with two sets of self-attested photocopies.
								Scanned photo and signature to be uploaded before DV.
								No additional time provided for missing documents.
							
							
							Outcome: Failure to produce valid documents results in disqualification.
						

						5. Medical Examination (ME)

						
							Purpose: Ensure A-1 medical standard compliance.
							Standards:
							
								General Fitness: Physically fit in all respects.
								Vision Standards:
								
									Distant Vision: 6/6, 6/6 without glasses (fogging test: must not accept +2D).
									Near Vision: Sn. 0.6, 0.6 without glasses.
									Colour Vision, Binocular Vision, Field of Vision, Night Vision: Normal.
								
								
								Note: Candidates with LASIK or corrective eye surgeries are ineligible.
							
							
							Process:
							
								Conducted by Railway Administration.
								One appeal allowed if failing initial examination (with charges).
								No alternative appointment for medical failures.
							
							
						

						
						Syllabus

						1. CBT-1 Syllabus

						CBT-1 tests general awareness, reasoning, and quantitative aptitude at a 10th-standard level.

						
							Mathematics:

							
								Number System
								BODMAS
								Decimals, Fractions
								LCM, HCF
								Ratio and Proportion
								Percentages
								Mensuration
								Time and Work
								Time and Distance
								Simple and Compound Interest
								Profit and Loss
								Algebra
								Geometry, Trigonometry
								Elementary Statistics
								Square Root
								Age Calculations
								Calendar, Clock
								Pipes and Cisterns
							
							
							General Intelligence and Reasoning:
							
								Analogies
								Alphabetical and Number Series
								Coding and Decoding
								Mathematical Operations
								Relationships
								Syllogism
								Jumbling
								Venn Diagram
								Data Interpretation and Sufficiency
								Conclusions, Decision Making
								Similarities, Differences
								Analytical Reasoning
								Classification
								Directions
								Statement – Arguments, Assumptions
							
							
							General Science:
							
								Physics, Chemistry, Life Sciences (10th standard CBSE syllabus).
								Key Topics:
								
									Mechanics
									Heat, Thermodynamics
									Electricity, Magnetism
									Optics
									Atomic Structure
									Chemical Reactions
									Organic Chemistry
									Human Body, Health
									Environment, Ecology
								
								
							
							
							General Awareness and Current Affairs:
							
								Science and Technology
								Sports
								Culture
								Personalities
								Economics
								Politics
								National and International Events
							
							
						

						2. CBT-2 Syllabus

						CBT-2 includes two parts with advanced topics.

						
							Part A:

							
								Mathematics: Same as CBT-1 (higher difficulty).
								General Intelligence and Reasoning: Same as CBT-1 (increased complexity).
								Basic Science and Engineering:
								
									Engineering Drawing (Projections, Views, Instruments, Lines, Geometric Figures)
									Units, Measurements
									Mass, Weight, Density
									Work, Power, Energy
									Speed, Velocity
									Heat, Temperature
									Basic Electricity
									Levers, Simple Machines
									Occupational Safety, Health
									Environment Education
									IT Literacy
								
								
								General Awareness and Current Affairs: Same as CBT-1 (focus on recent developments).
							
							
							Part B (Trade-Specific):
							
								Relevant to ALP qualifications (ITI/Apprenticeship/Diploma).
								Trades:
								
									Fitter
									Electrician

If you've been waiting for a stable, government job with growth and benefits, now’s the time to act.

						The online application process begins on 12 April 2025 and the last date to register and pay the fee is 19 May 2025. Candidates aged between 18 to 30 years (for General category) are eligible to apply, with age relaxation provided for OBC (33 years) and SC/ST (35 years) categories as per government norms Candidates from different educational backgrounds, especially those with ITI, diploma, or engineering qualifications, are eligible to apply. Selection will be through CBT (Computer-Based Test), followed by an aptitude test and document verification.

						What makes this recruitment exciting is not just the number of posts, but the attractive salary, career progression, and the prestige of working with Indian Railways. Assistant Loco Pilots play a vital role in train operations, and the job offers both technical challenge and long-term security.

						To apply, candidates must visit the official website of their respective RRB zone (like RRB Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, etc.), complete the registration, upload necessary documents, and pay the application fee online.

						With competition expected to be high, it's important to apply early, prepare well, and keep checking the official websites for updates. Whether you're a fresher or looking for a government switch, RRB ALP 2025 is your chance to drive your career forward — quite literally!

						

						
						RRB ALP (CEN 01/2025) Exam Pattern and Syllabus

						Exam Pattern

						The recruitment process for the Assistant Loco Pilot (ALP) under Centralized Employment Notice (CEN) No. 01/2025 consists of the following stages:

						
							First Stage Computer Based Test (CBT-1)
							Second Stage Computer Based Test (CBT-2)
							Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT)
							Document Verification (DV)
							Medical Examination (ME)
						

						1. First Stage CBT (CBT-1)

						
							Purpose: Preliminary screening.
							Mode: Computer Based Test (CBT).
							Duration: 60 minutes (80 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe).
							Total Questions: 75 (Multiple Choice Questions).
							Total Marks: 75.
							Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
							Qualifying Marks:
							
								UR & EWS: 40%
								OBC (NCL): 30%
								SC: 30%
								ST: 25%
								2% relaxation for PwBD candidates in respective categories.
							
							
							Shortlisting: Candidates are shortlisted for CBT-2 at 15 times the number of vacancies per RRB (subject to variation). Marks are normalized for multi-shift exams.
						

						2. Second Stage CBT (CBT-2)

						
							Purpose: Detailed assessment of technical and general knowledge.
							Mode: Computer Based Test.
							Structure: Divided into two parts:
							
								Part A:
								
									Duration: 90 minutes (120 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe).
									Total Questions: 100.
									Total Marks: 100.
									Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
									Qualifying Marks:
									
										UR & EWS: 40%
										OBC (NCL): 30%
										SC: 30%
										ST: 25%
										2% relaxation for PwBD candidates.
									
									
								
								
								Part B:
								
									Purpose: Assess technical knowledge relevant to ALP.
									Duration: 60 minutes (80 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe).
									Total Questions: 75.
									Total Marks: 75.
									Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
									Qualifying Marks: 35% (no relaxation for any category).
								
								
							
							
							Shortlisting: Candidates qualifying in both Part A and Part B are eligible for CBAT.
						

						3. Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT)

						
							Purpose: Evaluate aptitude for safety-critical ALP role.
							Mode: Computer Based Test.
							Languages: English and Hindi only.
							Structure: Multiple test batteries assessing cognitive and psychomotor skills.
							Negative Marking: None.
							Qualifying Marks: Minimum 42 marks in each test battery (applicable to all candidates, no relaxation).
							Weightage:
							
								CBAT: 70%
								CBT-2 (Part A): 30% for final merit list.
							
							
							Shortlisting: Candidates are shortlisted for Document Verification based on combined performance.
						

						4. Document Verification (DV)

						
							Purpose: Verify eligibility through original documents.
							Requirements:
							
								Original certificates (educational, technical, caste, age, etc.) with two sets of self-attested photocopies.
								Scanned photo and signature to be uploaded before DV.
								No additional time provided for missing documents.
							
							
							Outcome: Failure to produce valid documents results in disqualification.
						

						5. Medical Examination (ME)

						
							Purpose: Ensure A-1 medical standard compliance.
							Standards:
							
								General Fitness: Physically fit in all respects.
								Vision Standards:
								
									Distant Vision: 6/6, 6/6 without glasses (fogging test: must not accept +2D).
									Near Vision: Sn. 0.6, 0.6 without glasses.
									Colour Vision, Binocular Vision, Field of Vision, Night Vision: Normal.
								
								
								Note: Candidates with LASIK or corrective eye surgeries are ineligible.
							
							
							Process:
							
								Conducted by Railway Administration.
								One appeal allowed if failing initial examination (with charges).
								No alternative appointment for medical failures.
							
							
						

						
						Syllabus

						1. CBT-1 Syllabus

						CBT-1 tests general awareness, reasoning, and quantitative aptitude at a 10th-standard level.

						
							Mathematics:

							
								Number System
								BODMAS

With 9,970 Assistant Loco Pilot (ALP) vacancies available, this is one of the biggest railway recruitments of the year. 						The online application process begins on 12 April 2025 and the last date to register and pay the fee is 19 May 2025. Candidates aged between 18 to 30 years (for General category) are eligible to apply, with age relaxation provided for OBC (33 years) and SC/ST (35 years) categories as per government norms Candidates from different educational backgrounds, especially those with ITI, diploma, or engineering qualifications, are eligible to apply. Selection will be through CBT (Computer-Based Test), followed by an aptitude test and document verification.

						What makes this recruitment exciting is not just the number of posts, but the attractive salary, career progression, and the prestige of working with Indian Railways. Assistant Loco Pilots play a vital role in train operations, and the job offers both technical challenge and long-term security.

						To apply, candidates must visit the official website of their respective RRB zone (like RRB Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, etc.), complete the registration, upload necessary documents, and pay the application fee online.

						With competition expected to be high, it's important to apply early, prepare well, and keep checking the official websites for updates. Whether you're a fresher or looking for a government switch, RRB ALP 2025 is your chance to drive your career forward — quite literally!

						

						
						RRB ALP (CEN 01/2025) Exam Pattern and Syllabus

						Exam Pattern

						The recruitment process for the Assistant Loco Pilot (ALP) under Centralized Employment Notice (CEN) No. 01/2025 consists of the following stages:

						
							First Stage Computer Based Test (CBT-1)
							Second Stage Computer Based Test (CBT-2)
							Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT)
							Document Verification (DV)
							Medical Examination (ME)
						

						1. First Stage CBT (CBT-1)

						
							Purpose: Preliminary screening.
							Mode: Computer Based Test (CBT).
							Duration: 60 minutes (80 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe).
							Total Questions: 75 (Multiple Choice Questions).
							Total Marks: 75.
							Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
							Qualifying Marks:
							
								UR & EWS: 40%
								OBC (NCL): 30%
								SC: 30%
								ST: 25%
								2% relaxation for PwBD candidates in respective categories.
							
							
							Shortlisting: Candidates are shortlisted for CBT-2 at 15 times the number of vacancies per RRB (subject to variation). Marks are normalized for multi-shift exams.
						

						2. Second Stage CBT (CBT-2)

						
							Purpose: Detailed assessment of technical and general knowledge.
							Mode: Computer Based Test.
							Structure: Divided into two parts:
							
								Part A:
								
									Duration: 90 minutes (120 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe).
									Total Questions: 100.
									Total Marks: 100.
									Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
									Qualifying Marks:
									
										UR & EWS: 40%
										OBC (NCL): 30%
										SC: 30%
										ST: 25%
										2% relaxation for PwBD candidates.
									
									
								
								
								Part B:
								
									Purpose: Assess technical knowledge relevant to ALP.
									Duration: 60 minutes (80 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe).
									Total Questions: 75.
									Total Marks: 75.
									Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
									Qualifying Marks: 35% (no relaxation for any category).
								
								
							
							
							Shortlisting: Candidates qualifying in both Part A and Part B are eligible for CBAT.
						

						3. Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT)

						
							Purpose: Evaluate aptitude for safety-critical ALP role.
							Mode: Computer Based Test.
							Languages: English and Hindi only.
							Structure: Multiple test batteries assessing cognitive and psychomotor skills.
							Negative Marking: None.
							Qualifying Marks: Minimum 42 marks in each test battery (applicable to all candidates, no relaxation).
							Weightage:
							
								CBAT: 70%
								CBT-2 (Part A): 30% for final merit list.
							
							
							Shortlisting: Candidates are shortlisted for Document Verification based on combined performance.
						

						4. Document Verification (DV)

						
							Purpose: Verify eligibility through original documents.
							Requirements:
							
								Original certificates (educational, technical, caste, age, etc.) with two sets of self-attested photocopies.
								Scanned photo and signature to be uploaded before DV.
								No additional time provided for missing documents.
							
							
							Outcome: Failure to produce valid documents results in disqualification.
						

						5. Medical Examination (ME)

						
							Purpose: Ensure A-1 medical standard compliance.
							Standards:
							
								General Fitness: Physically fit in all respects.
								Vision Standards:
								
									Distant Vision: 6/6, 6/6 without glasses (fogging test: must not accept +2D).
									Near Vision: Sn. 0.6, 0.6 without glasses.
									Colour Vision, Binocular Vision, Field of Vision, Night Vision: Normal.
								
								
								Note: Candidates with LASIK or corrective eye surgeries are ineligible.
							
							
							Process:
							
								Conducted by Railway Administration.
								One appeal allowed if failing initial examination (with charges).
								No alternative appointment for medical failures.
							
							
						

						
						Syllabus

						1. CBT-1 Syllabus

						CBT-1 tests general awareness, reasoning, and quantitative aptitude at a 10th-standard level.

						
							Mathematics:

							
								Number System
								BODMAS
								Decimals, Fractions
								LCM, HCF
								Ratio and Proportion
								Percentages
								Mensuration
								Time and Work
								Time and Distance
								Simple and Compound Interest
								Profit and Loss
								Algebra
								Geometry, Trigonometry
								Elementary Statistics
								Square Root
								Age Calculations
								Calendar, Clock
								Pipes and Cisterns
							
							
							General Intelligence and Reasoning:
							
								Analogies
								Alphabetical and Number Series
								Coding and Decoding
								Mathematical Operations
								Relationships
								Syllogism
								Jumbling
								Venn Diagram
								Data Interpretation and Sufficiency
								Conclusions, Decision Making
								Similarities, Differences
								Analytical Reasoning
								Classification
								Directions
								Statement – Arguments, Assumptions
							
							
							General Science:
							
								Physics, Chemistry, Life Sciences (10th standard CBSE syllabus).
								Key Topics:
								
									Mechanics
									Heat, Thermodynamics
									Electricity, Magnetism
									Optics
									Atomic Structure
									Chemical Reactions
									Organic Chemistry
									Human Body, Health
									Environment, Ecology
								
								
							
							
							General Awareness and Current Affairs:
							
								Science and Technology
								Sports
								Culture
								Personalities
								Economics
								Politics
								National and International Events
							
							
						

						2. CBT-2 Syllabus

						CBT-2 includes two parts with advanced topics.

						
							Part A:

							
								Mathematics: Same as CBT-1 (higher difficulty).
								General Intelligence and Reasoning: Same as CBT-1 (increased complexity).
								Basic Science and Engineering:
								
									Engineering Drawing (Projections, Views, Instruments, Lines, Geometric Figures)
									Units, Measurements
									Mass, Weight, Density
									Work, Power, Energy
									Speed, Velocity
									Heat, Temperature
									Basic Electricity
									Levers, Simple Machines
									Occupational Safety, Health
									Environment Education
									IT Literacy
								
								
								General Awareness and Current Affairs: Same as CBT-1 (focus on recent developments).
							
							
							Part B (Trade-Specific):
							
								Relevant to ALP qualifications (ITI/Apprenticeship/Diploma).
								Trades:
								
									Fitter
									Electrician
									Instrument Mechanic
									Millwright/Maintenance Mechanic
									Mechanic (Radio & TV)
									Electronics Mechanic
									Mechanic (Motor Vehicle)
									Wireman
									Tractor Mechanic
									Armature & Coil Winder
									Mechanic (Diesel)
									Heat Engine
									Turner
									Machinist
									Refrigeration & Air-Conditioning Mechanic
								
								
								Engineering Disciplines:
								
									Mechanical
									Electrical
									Electronics
									Automobile
								
								
								Topics:
								
									Core concepts of the trade/discipline.
									Locomotive operations, maintenance.
									Safety protocols, tools, equipment.
								
								
							
							
						

						3. CBAT Syllabus

						
							Purpose: Assess psychomotor and cognitive skills for safety-critical roles.
							Topics:
							
								Memory: Pattern/sequence recall.
								Concentration: Attention under time constraints.
								Perception: Speed, accuracy in visual stimuli.
								Reasoning: Logical decision-making.
								Motor Skills: Hand-eye coordination, reaction time.
							
							
							Note: Practice aptitude tests for railway safety roles.

						RRB ALP (CEN 01/2025) Exam Pattern and Syllabus

						Exam Pattern

						The recruitment process for the Assistant Loco Pilot (ALP) under Centralized Employment Notice (CEN) No. 01/2025 consists of the following stages:

						
							First Stage Computer Based Test (CBT-1)
							Second Stage Computer Based Test (CBT-2)
							Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT)
							Document Verification (DV)
							Medical Examination (ME)
						

						1. First Stage CBT (CBT-1)

						
							Purpose: Preliminary screening.
							Mode: Computer Based Test (CBT).
							Duration: 60 minutes (80 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe).
							Total Questions: 75 (Multiple Choice Questions).
							Total Marks: 75.
							Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
							Qualifying Marks:
							
								UR & EWS: 40%
								OBC (NCL): 30%
								SC: 30%
								ST: 25%
								2% relaxation for PwBD candidates in respective categories.
							
							
							Shortlisting: Candidates are shortlisted for CBT-2 at 15 times the number of vacancies per RRB (subject to variation). Marks are normalized for multi-shift exams.
						

						2. Second Stage CBT (CBT-2)

						
							Purpose: Detailed assessment of technical and general knowledge.
							Mode: Computer Based Test.
							Structure: Divided into two parts:
							
								Part A:
								
									Duration: 90 minutes (120 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe).
									Total Questions: 100.
									Total Marks: 100.
									Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
									Qualifying Marks:
									
										UR & EWS: 40%
										OBC (NCL): 30%
										SC: 30%
										ST: 25%
										2% relaxation for PwBD candidates.
									
									
								
								
								Part B:
								
									Purpose: Assess technical knowledge relevant to ALP.
									Duration: 60 minutes (80 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe).
									Total Questions: 75.
									Total Marks: 75.
									Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
									Qualifying Marks: 35% (no relaxation for any category).
								
								
							
							
							Shortlisting: Candidates qualifying in both Part A and Part B are eligible for CBAT.
						

						3. Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT)

						
							Purpose: Evaluate aptitude for safety-critical ALP role.
							Mode: Computer Based Test.
							Languages: English and Hindi only.
							Structure: Multiple test batteries assessing cognitive and psychomotor skills.
							Negative Marking: None.
							Qualifying Marks: Minimum 42 marks in each test battery (applicable to all candidates, no relaxation).
							Weightage:
							
								CBAT: 70%
								CBT-2 (Part A): 30% for final merit list.
							
							
							Shortlisting: Candidates are shortlisted for Document Verification based on combined performance.
						

						4. Document Verification (DV)

						
							Purpose: Verify eligibility through original documents.
							Requirements:
							
								Original certificates (educational, technical, caste, age, etc.) with two sets of self-attested photocopies.
								Scanned photo and signature to be uploaded before DV.
								No additional time provided for missing documents.
							
							
							Outcome: Failure to produce valid documents results in disqualification.
						

						5. Medical Examination (ME)

						
							Purpose: Ensure A-1 medical standard compliance.
							Standards:
							
								General Fitness: Physically fit in all respects.
								Vision Standards:
								
									Distant Vision: 6/6, 6/6 without glasses (fogging test: must not accept +2D).
									Near Vision: Sn. 0.6, 0.6 without glasses.
									Colour Vision, Binocular Vision, Field of Vision, Night Vision: Normal.
								
								
								Note: Candidates with LASIK or corrective eye surgeries are ineligible.
							
							
							Process:
							
								Conducted by Railway Administration.
								One appeal allowed if failing initial examination (with charges).
								No alternative appointment for medical failures.
							
							
						

						
						Syllabus

						1. CBT-1 Syllabus

						CBT-1 tests general awareness, reasoning, and quantitative aptitude at a 10th-standard level.

						
							Mathematics:

							
								Number System
								BODMAS
								Decimals, Fractions
								LCM, HCF
								Ratio and Proportion
								Percentages
								Mensuration
								Time and Work
								Time and Distance
								Simple and Compound Interest
								Profit and Loss
								Algebra
								Geometry, Trigonometry
								Elementary Statistics
								Square Root
								Age Calculations
								Calendar, Clock
								Pipes and Cisterns
							
							
							General Intelligence and Reasoning:
							
								Analogies
								Alphabetical and Number Series
								Coding and Decoding
								Mathematical Operations
								Relationships
								Syllogism
								Jumbling
								Venn Diagram
								Data Interpretation and Sufficiency
								Conclusions, Decision Making
								Similarities, Differences
								Analytical Reasoning
								Classification
								Directions
								Statement – Arguments, Assumptions
							
							
							General Science:
							
								Physics, Chemistry, Life Sciences (10th standard CBSE syllabus).
								Key Topics:
								
									Mechanics
									Heat, Thermodynamics
									Electricity, Magnetism
									Optics
									Atomic Structure
									Chemical Reactions
									Organic Chemistry
									Human Body, Health
									Environment, Ecology
								
								
							
							
							General Awareness and Current Affairs:
							
								Science and Technology
								Sports
								Culture
								Personalities
								Economics
								Politics
								National and International Events
							
							
						

						2. CBT-2 Syllabus

						CBT-2 includes two parts with advanced topics.

						
							Part A:

							
								Mathematics: Same as CBT-1 (higher difficulty).
								General Intelligence and Reasoning: Same as CBT-1 (increased complexity).
								Basic Science and Engineering:
								
									Engineering Drawing (Projections, Views, Instruments, Lines, Geometric Figures)
									Units, Measurements
									Mass, Weight, Density
									Work, Power, Energy
									Speed, Velocity
									Heat, Temperature
									Basic Electricity
									Levers, Simple Machines
									Occupational Safety, Health
									Environment Education
									IT Literacy
								
								
								General Awareness and Current Affairs: Same as CBT-1 (focus on recent developments).
							
							
							Part B (Trade-Specific):
							
								Relevant to ALP qualifications (ITI/Apprenticeship/Diploma).
								Trades:
								
									Fitter
									Electrician
									Instrument Mechanic
									Millwright/Maintenance Mechanic
									Mechanic (Radio & TV)
									Electronics Mechanic
									Mechanic (Motor Vehicle)
									Wireman
									Tractor Mechanic
									Armature & Coil Winder
									Mechanic (Diesel)
									Heat Engine
									Turner
									Machinist
									Refrigeration & Air-Conditioning Mechanic
								
								
								Engineering Disciplines:
								
									Mechanical
									Electrical
									Electronics
									Automobile
								
								
								Topics:
								
									Core concepts of the trade/discipline.
									Locomotive operations, maintenance.
									Safety protocols, tools, equipment.
								
								
							
							
						

						3. CBAT Syllabus

						
							Purpose: Assess psychomotor and cognitive skills for safety-critical roles.
							Topics:
							
								Memory: Pattern/sequence recall.
								Concentration: Attention under time constraints.
								Perception: Speed, accuracy in visual stimuli.
								Reasoning: Logical decision-making.
								Motor Skills: Hand-eye coordination, reaction time.
							
							
							Note: Practice aptitude tests for railway safety roles.

						RRB ALP (CEN 01/2025) Exam Pattern and Syllabus

						Exam Pattern

						The recruitment process for the Assistant Loco Pilot (ALP) under Centralized Employment Notice (CEN) No. 01/2025 consists of the following stages:

						
							First Stage Computer Based Test (CBT-1)
							Second Stage Computer Based Test (CBT-2)
							Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT)
							Document Verification (DV)
							Medical Examination (ME)
						

						1. First Stage CBT (CBT-1)

						
							Purpose: Preliminary screening.
							Mode: Computer Based Test (CBT).
							Duration: 60 minutes (80 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe).
							Total Questions: 75 (Multiple Choice Questions).
							Total Marks: 75.
							Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
							Qualifying Marks:
							
								UR & EWS: 40%
								OBC (NCL): 30%
								SC: 30%
								ST: 25%
								2% relaxation for PwBD candidates in respective categories.
							
							
							Shortlisting: Candidates are shortlisted for CBT-2 at 15 times the number of vacancies per RRB (subject to variation). Marks are normalized for multi-shift exams.
						

						2. Second Stage CBT (CBT-2)

						
							Purpose: Detailed assessment of technical and general knowledge.
							Mode: Computer Based Test.
							Structure: Divided into two parts:
							
								Part A:
								
									Duration: 90 minutes (120 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe).
									Total Questions: 100.
									Total Marks: 100.
									Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
									Qualifying Marks:
									
										UR & EWS: 40%
										OBC (NCL): 30%
										SC: 30%
										ST: 25%
										2% relaxation for PwBD candidates.
									
									
								
								
								Part B:
								
									Purpose: Assess technical knowledge relevant to ALP.
									Duration: 60 minutes (80 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe).
									Total Questions: 75.
									Total Marks: 75.
									Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
									Qualifying Marks: 35% (no relaxation for any category).
								
								
							
							
							Shortlisting: Candidates qualifying in both Part A and Part B are eligible for CBAT.
						

						3. Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT)

						
							Purpose: Evaluate aptitude for safety-critical ALP role.
							Mode: Computer Based Test.
							Languages: English and Hindi only.
							Structure: Multiple test batteries assessing cognitive and psychomotor skills.
							Negative Marking: None.
							Qualifying Marks: Minimum 42 marks in each test battery (applicable to all candidates, no relaxation).
							Weightage:
							
								CBAT: 70%
								CBT-2 (Part A): 30% for final merit list.
							
							
							Shortlisting: Candidates are shortlisted for Document Verification based on combined performance.
						

						4. Document Verification (DV)

						
							Purpose: Verify eligibility through original documents.
							Requirements:
							
								Original certificates (educational, technical, caste, age, etc.) with two sets of self-attested photocopies.
								Scanned photo and signature to be uploaded before DV.
								No additional time provided for missing documents.
							
							
							Outcome: Failure to produce valid documents results in disqualification.
						

						5. Medical Examination (ME)

						
							Purpose: Ensure A-1 medical standard compliance.
							Standards:
							
								General Fitness: Physically fit in all respects.
								Vision Standards:
								
									Distant Vision: 6/6, 6/6 without glasses (fogging test: must not accept +2D).
									Near Vision: Sn. 0.6, 0.6 without glasses.
									Colour Vision, Binocular Vision, Field of Vision, Night Vision: Normal.
								
								
								Note: Candidates with LASIK or corrective eye surgeries are ineligible.
							
							
							Process:
							
								Conducted by Railway Administration.
								One appeal allowed if failing initial examination (with charges).
								No alternative appointment for medical failures.
							
							
						

						
						Syllabus

						1. CBT-1 Syllabus

						CBT-1 tests general awareness, reasoning, and quantitative aptitude at a 10th-standard level.

						
							Mathematics:

							
								Number System
								BODMAS
								Decimals, Fractions
								LCM, HCF
								Ratio and Proportion
								Percentages
								Mensuration
								Time and Work
								Time and Distance
								Simple and Compound Interest
								Profit and Loss
								Algebra
								Geometry, Trigonometry
								Elementary Statistics
								Square Root
								Age Calculations
								Calendar, Clock
								Pipes and Cisterns
							
							
							General Intelligence and Reasoning:
							
								Analogies
								Alphabetical and Number Series
								Coding and Decoding
								Mathematical Operations
								Relationships
								Syllogism
								Jumbling
								Venn Diagram
								Data Interpretation and Sufficiency
								Conclusions, Decision Making
								Similarities, Differences
								Analytical Reasoning
								Classification
								Directions
								Statement – Arguments, Assumptions
							
							
							General Science:
							
								Physics, Chemistry, Life Sciences (10th standard CBSE syllabus).
								Key Topics:
								
									Mechanics
									Heat, Thermodynamics
									Electricity, Magnetism
									Optics
									Atomic Structure
									Chemical Reactions
									Organic Chemistry
									Human Body, Health
									Environment, Ecology
								
								
							
							
							General Awareness and Current Affairs:
							
								Science and Technology
								Sports
								Culture
								Personalities
								Economics
								Politics
								National and International Events
							
							
						

						2. CBT-2 Syllabus

						CBT-2 includes two parts with advanced topics.

						
							Part A:

							
								Mathematics: Same as CBT-1 (higher difficulty).
								General Intelligence and Reasoning: Same as CBT-1 (increased complexity).
								Basic Science and Engineering:
								
									Engineering Drawing (Projections, Views, Instruments, Lines, Geometric Figures)
									Units, Measurements
									Mass, Weight, Density
									Work, Power, Energy
									Speed, Velocity
									Heat, Temperature
									Basic Electricity
									Levers, Simple Machines
									Occupational Safety, Health
									Environment Education
									IT Literacy
								
								
								General Awareness and Current Affairs: Same as CBT-1 (focus on recent developments).
							
							
							Part B (Trade-Specific):
							
								Relevant to ALP qualifications (ITI/Apprenticeship/Diploma).
								Trades:
								
									Fitter
									Electrician
									Instrument Mechanic
									Millwright/Maintenance Mechanic
									Mechanic (Radio & TV)
									Electronics Mechanic
									Mechanic (Motor Vehicle)
									Wireman
									Tractor Mechanic
									Armature & Coil Winder
									Mechanic (Diesel)
									Heat Engine
									Turner
									Machinist
									Refrigeration & Air-Conditioning Mechanic
								
								
								Engineering Disciplines:
								
									Mechanical
									Electrical
									Electronics
									Automobile
								
								
								Topics:
								
									Core concepts of the trade/discipline.
									Locomotive operations, maintenance.
									Safety protocols, tools, equipment.
								
								
							
							
						

						3. CBAT Syllabus

						
							Purpose: Assess psychomotor and cognitive skills for safety-critical roles.
							Topics:
							
								Memory: Pattern/sequence recall.
								Concentration: Attention under time constraints.
								Perception: Speed, accuracy in visual stimuli.
								Reasoning: Logical decision-making.
								Motor Skills: Hand-eye coordination, reaction time.
							
							
							Note: Practice aptitude tests for railway safety roles.

						RRB ALP (CEN 01/2025) Exam Pattern and Syllabus

						Exam Pattern

						The recruitment process for the Assistant Loco Pilot (ALP) under Centralized Employment Notice (CEN) No. 01/2025 consists of the following stages:

						
							First Stage Computer Based Test (CBT-1)
							Second Stage Computer Based Test (CBT-2)
							Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT)
							Document Verification (DV)
							Medical Examination (ME)
						

						1. First Stage CBT (CBT-1)

						
							Purpose: Preliminary screening.
							Mode: Computer Based Test (CBT).
							Duration: 60 minutes (80 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe).
							Total Questions: 75 (Multiple Choice Questions).
							Total Marks: 75.
							Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
							Qualifying Marks:
							
								UR & EWS: 40%
								OBC (NCL): 30%
								SC: 30%
								ST: 25%
								2% relaxation for PwBD candidates in respective categories.
							
							
							Shortlisting: Candidates are shortlisted for CBT-2 at 15 times the number of vacancies per RRB (subject to variation). Marks are normalized for multi-shift exams.
						

						2. Second Stage CBT (CBT-2)

						
							Purpose: Detailed assessment of technical and general knowledge.
							Mode: Computer Based Test.
							Structure: Divided into two parts:
							
								Part A:
								
									Duration: 90 minutes (120 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe).
									Total Questions: 100.
									Total Marks: 100.
									Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
									Qualifying Marks:
									
										UR & EWS: 40%
										OBC (NCL): 30%
										SC: 30%
										ST: 25%
										2% relaxation for PwBD candidates.
									
									
								
								
								Part B:
								
									Purpose: Assess technical knowledge relevant to ALP.
									Duration: 60 minutes (80 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe).
									Total Questions: 75.
									Total Marks: 75.
									Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
									Qualifying Marks: 35% (no relaxation for any category).
								
								
							
							
							Shortlisting: Candidates qualifying in both Part A and Part B are eligible for CBAT.
						

						3. Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT)

						
							Purpose: Evaluate aptitude for safety-critical ALP role.
							Mode: Computer Based Test.
							Languages: English and Hindi only.
							Structure: Multiple test batteries assessing cognitive and psychomotor skills.
							Negative Marking: None.
							Qualifying Marks: Minimum 42 marks in each test battery (applicable to all candidates, no relaxation).
							Weightage:
							
								CBAT: 70%
								CBT-2 (Part A): 30% for final merit list.
							
							
							Shortlisting: Candidates are shortlisted for Document Verification based on combined performance.
						

						4. Document Verification (DV)

						
							Purpose: Verify eligibility through original documents.
							Requirements:
							
								Original certificates (educational, technical, caste, age, etc.) with two sets of self-attested photocopies.
								Scanned photo and signature to be uploaded before DV.
								No additional time provided for missing documents.
							
							
							Outcome: Failure to produce valid documents results in disqualification.
						

						5. Medical Examination (ME)

						
							Purpose: Ensure A-1 medical standard compliance.
							Standards:
							
								General Fitness: Physically fit in all respects.
								Vision Standards:
								
									Distant Vision: 6/6, 6/6 without glasses (fogging test: must not accept +2D).
									Near Vision: Sn. 0.6, 0.6 without glasses.
									Colour Vision, Binocular Vision, Field of Vision, Night Vision: Normal.
								
								
								Note: Candidates with LASIK or corrective eye surgeries are ineligible.
							
							
							Process:
							
								Conducted by Railway Administration.
								One appeal allowed if failing initial examination (with charges).
								No alternative appointment for medical failures.
							
							
						

						
						Syllabus

						1. CBT-1 Syllabus

						CBT-1 tests general awareness, reasoning, and quantitative aptitude at a 10th-standard level.

						
							Mathematics:

							
								Number System
								BODMAS
								Decimals, Fractions
								LCM, HCF
								Ratio and Proportion
								Percentages
								Mensuration
								Time and Work
								Time and Distance
								Simple and Compound Interest
								Profit and Loss
								Algebra
								Geometry, Trigonometry
								Elementary Statistics
								Square Root
								Age Calculations
								Calendar, Clock
								Pipes and Cisterns
							
							
							General Intelligence and Reasoning:
							
								Analogies
								Alphabetical and Number Series
								Coding and Decoding
								Mathematical Operations
								Relationships
								Syllogism
								Jumbling
								Venn Diagram
								Data Interpretation and Sufficiency
								Conclusions, Decision Making
								Similarities, Differences
								Analytical Reasoning
								Classification
								Directions
								Statement – Arguments, Assumptions
							
							
							General Science:
							
								Physics, Chemistry, Life Sciences (10th standard CBSE syllabus).
								Key Topics:
								
									Mechanics
									Heat, Thermodynamics
									Electricity, Magnetism
									Optics
									Atomic Structure
									Chemical Reactions
									Organic Chemistry
									Human Body, Health
									Environment, Ecology
								
								
							
							
							General Awareness and Current Affairs:
							
								Science and Technology
								Sports
								Culture
								Personalities
								Economics
								Politics
								National and International Events
							
							
						

						2. CBT-2 Syllabus

						CBT-2 includes two parts with advanced topics.

						
							Part A:

							
								Mathematics: Same as CBT-1 (higher difficulty).
								General Intelligence and Reasoning: Same as CBT-1 (increased complexity).
								Basic Science and Engineering:
								
									Engineering Drawing (Projections, Views, Instruments, Lines, Geometric Figures)
									Units, Measurements
									Mass, Weight, Density
									Work, Power, Energy
									Speed, Velocity
									Heat, Temperature
									Basic Electricity
									Levers, Simple Machines
									Occupational Safety, Health
									Environment Education
									IT Literacy
								
								
								General Awareness and Current Affairs: Same as CBT-1 (focus on recent developments).
							
							
							Part B (Trade-Specific):
							
								Relevant to ALP qualifications (ITI/Apprenticeship/Diploma).
								Trades:
								
									Fitter
									Electrician
									Instrument Mechanic
									Millwright/Maintenance Mechanic
									Mechanic (Radio & TV)
									Electronics Mechanic
									Mechanic (Motor Vehicle)
									Wireman
									Tractor Mechanic
									Armature & Coil Winder
									Mechanic (Diesel)
									Heat Engine
									Turner
									Machinist
									Refrigeration & Air-Conditioning Mechanic
								
								
								Engineering Disciplines:
								
									Mechanical
									Electrical
									Electronics
									Automobile
								
								
								Topics:
								
									Core concepts of the trade/discipline.
									Locomotive operations, maintenance.
									Safety protocols, tools, equipment.
								
								
							
							
						

						3. CBAT Syllabus

						
							Purpose: Assess psychomotor and cognitive skills for safety-critical roles.
							Topics:
							
								Memory: Pattern/sequence recall.
								Concentration: Attention under time constraints.
								Perception: Speed, accuracy in visual stimuli.
								Reasoning: Logical decision-making.
								Motor Skills: Hand-eye coordination, reaction time.
							
							
							Note: Practice aptitude tests for railway safety roles.

						RRB ALP (CEN 01/2025) Exam Pattern and Syllabus

						Exam Pattern

						The recruitment process for the Assistant Loco Pilot (ALP) under Centralized Employment Notice (CEN) No. 01/2025 consists of the following stages:

						
							First Stage Computer Based Test (CBT-1)
							Second Stage Computer Based Test (CBT-2)
							Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT)
							Document Verification (DV)
							Medical Examination (ME)
						

						1. First Stage CBT (CBT-1)

						
							Purpose: Preliminary screening.
							Mode: Computer Based Test (CBT).
							Duration: 60 minutes (80 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe).
							Total Questions: 75 (Multiple Choice Questions).
							Total Marks: 75.
							Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
							Qualifying Marks:
							
								UR & EWS: 40%
								OBC (NCL): 30%
								SC: 30%
								ST: 25%
								2% relaxation for PwBD candidates in respective categories.
							
							
							Shortlisting: Candidates are shortlisted for CBT-2 at 15 times the number of vacancies per RRB (subject to variation). Marks are normalized for multi-shift exams.
						

						2. Second Stage CBT (CBT-2)

						
							Purpose: Detailed assessment of technical and general knowledge.
							Mode: Computer Based Test.
							Structure: Divided into two parts:
							
								Part A:
								
									Duration: 90 minutes (120 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe).
									Total Questions: 100.
									Total Marks: 100.
									Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
									Qualifying Marks:
									
										UR & EWS: 40%
										OBC (NCL): 30%
										SC: 30%
										ST: 25%
										2% relaxation for PwBD candidates.
									
									
								
								
								Part B:
								
									Purpose: Assess technical knowledge relevant to ALP.
									Duration: 60 minutes (80 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe).
									Total Questions: 75.
									Total Marks: 75.
									Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
									Qualifying Marks: 35% (no relaxation for any category).
								
								
							
							
							Shortlisting: Candidates qualifying in both Part A and Part B are eligible for CBAT.
						

						3. Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT)

						
							Purpose: Evaluate aptitude for safety-critical ALP role.
							Mode: Computer Based Test.
							Languages: English and Hindi only.
							Structure: Multiple test batteries assessing cognitive and psychomotor skills.
							Negative Marking: None.
							Qualifying Marks: Minimum 42 marks in each test battery (applicable to all candidates, no relaxation).
							Weightage:
							
								CBAT: 70%
								CBT-2 (Part A): 30% for final merit list.
							
							
							Shortlisting: Candidates are shortlisted for Document Verification based on combined performance.
						

						4. Document Verification (DV)

						
							Purpose: Verify eligibility through original documents.
							Requirements:
							
								Original certificates (educational, technical, caste, age, etc.) with two sets of self-attested photocopies.
								Scanned photo and signature to be uploaded before DV.
								No additional time provided for missing documents.
							
							
							Outcome: Failure to produce valid documents results in disqualification.
						

						5. Medical Examination (ME)

						
							Purpose: Ensure A-1 medical standard compliance.
							Standards:
							
								General Fitness: Physically fit in all respects.
								Vision Standards:
								
									Distant Vision: 6/6, 6/6 without glasses (fogging test: must not accept +2D).
									Near Vision: Sn. 0.6, 0.6 without glasses.
									Colour Vision, Binocular Vision, Field of Vision, Night Vision: Normal.
								
								
								Note: Candidates with LASIK or corrective eye surgeries are ineligible.
							
							
							Process:
							
								Conducted by Railway Administration.
								One appeal allowed if failing initial examination (with charges).
								No alternative appointment for medical failures.
							
							
						

						
						Syllabus

						1. CBT-1 Syllabus

						CBT-1 tests general awareness, reasoning, and quantitative aptitude at a 10th-standard level.

						
							Mathematics:

							
								Number System
								BODMAS
								Decimals, Fractions
								LCM, HCF
								Ratio and Proportion
								Percentages
								Mensuration
								Time and Work
								Time and Distance
								Simple and Compound Interest
								Profit and Loss
								Algebra
								Geometry, Trigonometry
								Elementary Statistics
								Square Root
								Age Calculations
								Calendar, Clock
								Pipes and Cisterns
							
							
							General Intelligence and Reasoning:
							
								Analogies
								Alphabetical and Number Series
								Coding and Decoding
								Mathematical Operations
								Relationships
								Syllogism
								Jumbling
								Venn Diagram
								Data Interpretation and Sufficiency
								Conclusions, Decision Making
								Similarities, Differences
								Analytical Reasoning
								Classification
								Directions
								Statement – Arguments, Assumptions
							
							
							General Science:
							
								Physics, Chemistry, Life Sciences (10th standard CBSE syllabus).
								Key Topics:
								
									Mechanics
									Heat, Thermodynamics
									Electricity, Magnetism
									Optics
									Atomic Structure
									Chemical Reactions
									Organic Chemistry
									Human Body, Health
									Environment, Ecology
								
								
							
							
							General Awareness and Current Affairs:
							
								Science and Technology
								Sports
								Culture
								Personalities
								Economics
								Politics
								National and International Events
							
							
						

						2. CBT-2 Syllabus

						CBT-2 includes two parts with advanced topics.

						
							Part A:

							
								Mathematics: Same as CBT-1 (higher difficulty).
								General Intelligence and Reasoning: Same as CBT-1 (increased complexity).
								Basic Science and Engineering:
								
									Engineering Drawing (Projections, Views, Instruments, Lines, Geometric Figures)
									Units, Measurements
									Mass, Weight, Density
									Work, Power, Energy
									Speed, Velocity
									Heat, Temperature
									Basic Electricity
									Levers, Simple Machines
									Occupational Safety, Health
									Environment Education
									IT Literacy
								
								
								General Awareness and Current Affairs: Same as CBT-1 (focus on recent developments).
							
							
							Part B (Trade-Specific):
							
								Relevant to ALP qualifications (ITI/Apprenticeship/Diploma).
								Trades:
								
									Fitter
									Electrician
									Instrument Mechanic
									Millwright/Maintenance Mechanic
									Mechanic (Radio & TV)
									Electronics Mechanic
									Mechanic (Motor Vehicle)
									Wireman
									Tractor Mechanic
									Armature & Coil Winder
									Mechanic (Diesel)
									Heat Engine
									Turner
									Machinist
									Refrigeration & Air-Conditioning Mechanic
								
								
								Engineering Disciplines:
								
									Mechanical
									Electrical
									Electronics
									Automobile
								
								
								Topics:
								
									Core concepts of the trade/discipline.
									Locomotive operations, maintenance.
									Safety protocols, tools, equipment.
								
								
							
							
						

						3. CBAT Syllabus

						
							Purpose: Assess psychomotor and cognitive skills for safety-critical roles.
							Topics:
							
								Memory: Pattern/sequence recall.
								Concentration: Attention under time constraints.
								Perception: Speed, accuracy in visual stimuli.
								Reasoning: Logical decision-making.
								Motor Skills: Hand-eye coordination, reaction time.
							
							
							Note: Practice aptitude tests for railway safety roles.

						What makes this recruitment exciting is not just the number of posts, but the attractive salary, career progression, and the prestige of working with Indian Railways. Assistant Loco Pilots play a vital role in train operations, and the job offers both technical challenge and long-term security.

						RRB ALP (CEN 01/2025) Exam Pattern and Syllabus

						Exam Pattern

						The recruitment process for the Assistant Loco Pilot (ALP) under Centralized Employment Notice (CEN) No. 01/2025 consists of the following stages:

						
							First Stage Computer Based Test (CBT-1)
							Second Stage Computer Based Test (CBT-2)
							Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT)
							Document Verification (DV)
							Medical Examination (ME)
						

						1. First Stage CBT (CBT-1)

						
							Purpose: Preliminary screening.
							Mode: Computer Based Test (CBT).
							Duration: 60 minutes (80 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe).
							Total Questions: 75 (Multiple Choice Questions).
							Total Marks: 75.
							Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
							Qualifying Marks:
							
								UR & EWS: 40%
								OBC (NCL): 30%
								SC: 30%
								ST: 25%
								2% relaxation for PwBD candidates in respective categories.
							
							
							Shortlisting: Candidates are shortlisted for CBT-2 at 15 times the number of vacancies per RRB (subject to variation). Marks are normalized for multi-shift exams.
						

						2. Second Stage CBT (CBT-2)

						
							Purpose: Detailed assessment of technical and general knowledge.
							Mode: Computer Based Test.
							Structure: Divided into two parts:
							
								Part A:
								
									Duration: 90 minutes (120 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe).
									Total Questions: 100.
									Total Marks: 100.
									Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
									Qualifying Marks:
									
										UR & EWS: 40%
										OBC (NCL): 30%
										SC: 30%
										ST: 25%
										2% relaxation for PwBD candidates.
									
									
								
								
								Part B:
								
									Purpose: Assess technical knowledge relevant to ALP.
									Duration: 60 minutes (80 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe).
									Total Questions: 75.
									Total Marks: 75.
									Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer.
									Qualifying Marks: 35% (no relaxation for any category).
								
								
							
							
							Shortlisting: Candidates qualifying in both Part A and Part B are eligible for CBAT.
						

						3. Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT)

						
							Purpose: Evaluate aptitude for safety-critical ALP role.
							Mode: Computer Based Test.
							Languages: English and Hindi only.
							Structure: Multiple test batteries assessing cognitive and psychomotor skills.
							Negative Marking: None.
							Qualifying Marks: Minimum 42 marks in each test battery (applicable to all candidates, no relaxation).
							Weightage:
							
								CBAT: 70%
								CBT-2 (Part A): 30% for final merit list.
							
							
							Shortlisting: Candidates are shortlisted for Document Verification based on combined performance.
						

						4. Document Verification (DV)

						
							Purpose: Verify eligibility through original documents.
							Requirements:
							
								Original certificates (educational, technical, caste, age, etc.) with two sets of self-attested photocopies.
								Scanned photo and signature to be uploaded before DV.
								No additional time provided for missing documents.
							
							
							Outcome: Failure to produce valid documents results in disqualification.
						

						5. Medical Examination (ME)

						
							Purpose: Ensure A-1 medical standard compliance.
							Standards:
							
								General Fitness: Physically fit in all respects.
								Vision Standards:
								
									Distant Vision: 6/6, 6/6 without glasses (fogging test: must not accept +2D).
									Near Vision: Sn. 0.6, 0.6 without glasses.
									Colour Vision, Binocular Vision, Field of Vision, Night Vision: Normal.
								
								
								Note: Candidates with LASIK or corrective eye surgeries are ineligible.
							
							
							Process:
							
								Conducted by Railway Administration.
								One appeal allowed if failing initial examination (with charges).
								No alternative appointment for medical failures.
							
							
						

						
						Syllabus

						1. CBT-1 Syllabus

						CBT-1 tests general awareness, reasoning, and quantitative aptitude at a 10th-standard level.

						
							Mathematics:

							
								Number System
								BODMAS
								Decimals, Fractions
								LCM, HCF
								Ratio and Proportion
								Percentages
								Mensuration
								Time and Work
								Time and Distance
								Simple and Compound Interest
								Profit and Loss
								Algebra
								Geometry, Trigonometry
								Elementary Statistics
								Square Root
								Age Calculations
								Calendar, Clock
								Pipes and Cisterns
							
							
							General Intelligence and Reasoning:
							
								Analogies
								Alphabetical and Number Series
								Coding and Decoding
								Mathematical Operations
								Relationships
								Syllogism
								Jumbling
								Venn Diagram
								Data Interpretation and Sufficiency
								Conclusions, Decision Making
								Similarities, Differences
								Analytical Reasoning
								Classification
								Directions
								Statement – Arguments, Assumptions
							
							
							General Science:
							
								Physics, Chemistry, Life Sciences (10th standard CBSE syllabus).
								Key Topics:
								
									Mechanics
									Heat, Thermodynamics
									Electricity, Magnetism
									Optics
									Atomic Structure
									Chemical Reactions
									Organic Chemistry
									Human Body, Health
									Environment, Ecology
								
								
							
							
							General Awareness and Current Affairs:
							
								Science and Technology
								Sports
								Culture
								Personalities
								Economics
								Politics
								National and International Events
							
							
						

						2. CBT-2 Syllabus

						CBT-2 includes two parts with advanced topics.

						
							Part A:

							
								Mathematics: Same as CBT-1 (higher difficulty).
								General Intelligence and Reasoning: Same as CBT-1 (increased complexity).
								Basic Science and Engineering:
								
									Engineering Drawing (Projections, Views, Instruments, Lines, Geometric Figures)
									Units, Measurements
									Mass, Weight, Density
									Work, Power, Energy
									Speed, Velocity
									Heat, Temperature
									Basic Electricity
									Levers, Simple Machines
									Occupational Safety, Health
									Environment Education
									IT Literacy
								
								
								General Awareness and Current Affairs: Same as CBT-1 (focus on recent developments).
							
							
							Part B (Trade-Specific):
							
								Relevant to ALP qualifications (ITI/Apprenticeship/Diploma).
								Trades:
								
									Fitter
									Electrician
									Instrument Mechanic
									Millwright/Maintenance Mechanic
									Mechanic (Radio & TV)
									Electronics Mechanic
									Mechanic (Motor Vehicle)
									Wireman
									Tractor Mechanic
									Armature & Coil Winder
									Mechanic (Diesel)
									Heat Engine
									Turner
									Machinist
									Refrigeration & Air-Conditioning Mechanic
								
								
								Engineering Disciplines:
								
									Mechanical
									Electrical
									Electronics
									Automobile
								
								
								Topics:
								
									Core concepts of the trade/discipline.
									Locomotive operations, maintenance.
									Safety protocols, tools, equipment.
								
								
							
							
						

						3. CBAT Syllabus

						
							Purpose: Assess psychomotor and cognitive skills for safety-critical roles.
							Topics:
							
								Memory: Pattern/sequence recall.
								Concentration: Attention under time constraints.
								Perception: Speed, accuracy in visual stimuli.
								Reasoning: Logical decision-making.
								Motor Skills: Hand-eye coordination, reaction time.
							
							
							Note: Practice aptitude tests for railway safety roles.

RRB ALP (CEN 01/2025) Exam Pattern and Syllabus Exam Pattern The recruitment process for the Assistant Loco Pilot (ALP) under Centralized Employment Notice (CEN) No. 01/2025 consists of the following stages: First Stage Computer Based Test (CBT-1) Second Stage Computer Based Test (CBT-2) Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT) Document Verification (DV) Medical Examination (ME) 1. First Stage CBT (CBT-1) Purpose: Preliminary screening. Mode: Computer Based Test (CBT). Duration: 60 minutes (80 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe). Total Questions: 75 (Multiple Choice Questions). Total Marks: 75. Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer. Qualifying Marks: UR & EWS: 40% OBC (NCL): 30% SC: 30% ST: 25% 2% relaxation for PwBD candidates in respective categories. Shortlisting: Candidates are shortlisted for CBT-2 at 15 times the number of vacancies per RRB (subject to variation). Marks are normalized for multi-shift exams. 2. Second Stage CBT (CBT-2) Purpose: Detailed assessment of technical and general knowledge. Mode: Computer Based Test. Structure: Divided into two parts: Part A: Duration: 90 minutes (120 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe). Total Questions: 100. Total Marks: 100. Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer. Qualifying Marks: UR & EWS: 40% OBC (NCL): 30% SC: 30% ST: 25% 2% relaxation for PwBD candidates. Part B: Purpose: Assess technical knowledge relevant to ALP. Duration: 60 minutes (80 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe). Total Questions: 75. Total Marks: 75. Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer. Qualifying Marks: 35% (no relaxation for any category). Shortlisting: Candidates qualifying in both Part A and Part B are eligible for CBAT. 3. Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT) Purpose: Evaluate aptitude for safety-critical ALP role. Mode: Computer Based Test. Languages: English and Hindi only. Structure: Multiple test batteries assessing cognitive and psychomotor skills. Negative Marking: None. Qualifying Marks: Minimum 42 marks in each test battery (applicable to all candidates, no relaxation). Weightage: CBAT: 70% CBT-2 (Part A): 30% for final merit list. Shortlisting: Candidates are shortlisted for Document Verification based on combined performance. 4. Document Verification (DV) Purpose: Verify eligibility through original documents. Requirements: Original certificates (educational, technical, caste, age, etc.) with two sets of self-attested photocopies. Scanned photo and signature to be uploaded before DV. No additional time provided for missing documents. Outcome: Failure to produce valid documents results in disqualification. 5. Medical Examination (ME) Purpose: Ensure A-1 medical standard compliance. Standards: General Fitness: Physically fit in all respects. Vision Standards: Distant Vision: 6/6, 6/6 without glasses (fogging test: must not accept +2D). Near Vision: Sn. 0.6, 0.6 without glasses. Colour Vision, Binocular Vision, Field of Vision, Night Vision: Normal. Note: Candidates with LASIK or corrective eye surgeries are ineligible. Process: Conducted by Railway Administration. One appeal allowed if failing initial examination (with charges). No alternative appointment for medical failures. Syllabus 1. CBT-1 Syllabus CBT-1 tests general awareness, reasoning, and quantitative aptitude at a 10th-standard level. Mathematics: Number System BODMAS Decimals, Fractions LCM, HCF Ratio and Proportion Percentages Mensuration Time and Work Time and Distance Simple and Compound Interest Profit and Loss Algebra Geometry, Trigonometry Elementary Statistics Square Root Age Calculations Calendar, Clock Pipes and Cisterns General Intelligence and Reasoning: Analogies Alphabetical and Number Series Coding and Decoding Mathematical Operations Relationships Syllogism Jumbling Venn Diagram Data Interpretation and Sufficiency Conclusions, Decision Making Similarities, Differences Analytical Reasoning Classification Directions Statement – Arguments, Assumptions General Science: Physics, Chemistry, Life Sciences (10th standard CBSE syllabus). Key Topics: Mechanics Heat, Thermodynamics Electricity, Magnetism Optics Atomic Structure Chemical Reactions Organic Chemistry Human Body, Health Environment, Ecology General Awareness and Current Affairs: Science and Technology Sports Culture Personalities Economics Politics National and International Events 2. CBT-2 Syllabus CBT-2 includes two parts with advanced topics. Part A: Mathematics: Same as CBT-1 (higher difficulty). General Intelligence and Reasoning: Same as CBT-1 (increased complexity). Basic Science and Engineering: Engineering Drawing (Projections, Views, Instruments, Lines, Geometric Figures) Units, Measurements Mass, Weight, Density Work, Power, Energy Speed, Velocity Heat, Temperature Basic Electricity Levers, Simple Machines Occupational Safety, Health Environment Education IT Literacy General Awareness and Current Affairs: Same as CBT-1 (focus on recent developments). Part B (Trade-Specific): Relevant to ALP qualifications (ITI/Apprenticeship/Diploma). Trades: Fitter Electrician Instrument Mechanic Millwright/Maintenance Mechanic Mechanic (Radio & TV) Electronics Mechanic Mechanic (Motor Vehicle) Wireman Tractor Mechanic Armature & Coil Winder Mechanic (Diesel) Heat Engine Turner Machinist Refrigeration & Air-Conditioning Mechanic Engineering Disciplines: Mechanical Electrical Electronics Automobile Topics: Core concepts of the trade/discipline. Locomotive operations, maintenance. Safety protocols, tools, equipment. 3. CBAT Syllabus Purpose: Assess psychomotor and cognitive skills for safety-critical roles. Topics: Memory: Pattern/sequence recall. Concentration: Attention under time constraints. Perception: Speed, accuracy in visual stimuli. Reasoning: Logical decision-making. Motor Skills: Hand-eye coordination, reaction time. RRB ALP (CEN 01/2025) Exam Pattern and Syllabus Exam Pattern The recruitment process for the Assistant Loco Pilot (ALP) under Centralized Employment Notice (CEN) No. 01/2025 consists of the following stages: First Stage Computer Based Test (CBT-1) Second Stage Computer Based Test (CBT-2) Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT) Document Verification (DV) Medical Examination (ME) 1. First Stage CBT (CBT-1) Purpose: Preliminary screening. Mode: Computer Based Test (CBT). Duration: 60 minutes (80 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe). Total Questions: 75 (Multiple Choice Questions). Total Marks: 75. Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer. Qualifying Marks: UR & EWS: 40% OBC (NCL): 30% SC: 30% ST: 25% 2% relaxation for PwBD candidates in respective categories. Shortlisting: Candidates are shortlisted for CBT-2 at 15 times the number of vacancies per RRB (subject to variation). Marks are normalized for multi-shift exams. 2. Second Stage CBT (CBT-2) Purpose: Detailed assessment of technical and general knowledge. Mode: Computer Based Test. Structure: Divided into two parts: Part A: Duration: 90 minutes (120 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe). Total Questions: 100. Total Marks: 100. Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer. Qualifying Marks: UR & EWS: 40% OBC (NCL): 30% SC: 30% ST: 25% 2% relaxation for PwBD candidates. Part B: Purpose: Assess technical knowledge relevant to ALP. Duration: 60 minutes (80 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates with scribe). Total Questions: 75. Total Marks: 75. Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer. Qualifying Marks: 35% (no relaxation for any category). Shortlisting: Candidates qualifying in both Part A and Part B are eligible for CBAT. 3. Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT) Purpose: Evaluate aptitude for safety-critical ALP role. Mode: Computer Based Test. Languages: English and Hindi only. Structure: Multiple test batteries assessing cognitive and psychomotor skills. Negative Marking: None. Qualifying Marks: Minimum 42 marks in each test battery (applicable to all candidates, no relaxation). Weightage: CBAT: 70% CBT-2 (Part A): 30% for final merit list. Shortlisting: Candidates are shortlisted for Document Verification based on combined performance. 4. Document Verification (DV) Purpose: Verify eligibility through original documents. Requirements: Original certificates (educational, technical, caste, age, etc.) with two sets of self-attested photocopies. Scanned photo and signature to be uploaded before DV. No additional time provided for missing documents. Outcome: Failure to produce valid documents results in disqualification. 5. Medical Examination (ME) Purpose: Ensure A-1 medical standard compliance. Standards: General Fitness: Physically fit in all respects. Vision Standards: Distant Vision: 6/6, 6/6 without glasses (fogging test: must not accept +2D). Near Vision: Sn. 0.6, 0.6 without glasses. Colour Vision, Binocular Vision, Field of Vision, Night Vision: Normal. Note: Candidates with LASIK or corrective eye surgeries are ineligible. Process: Conducted by Railway Administration. One appeal allowed if failing initial examination (with charges). No alternative appointment for medical failures. Syllabus 1. CBT-1 Syllabus CBT-1 tests general awareness, reasoning, and quantitative aptitude at a 10th-standard level. Mathematics: Number System BODMAS Decimals, Fractions LCM, HCF Ratio and Proportion Percentages Mensuration Time and Work Time and Distance Simple and Compound Interest Profit and Loss Algebra Geometry, Trigonometry Elementary Statistics Square Root Age Calculations Calendar, Clock Pipes and Cisterns General Intelligence and Reasoning: Analogies Alphabetical and Number Series Coding and Decoding Mathematical Operations Relationships Syllogism Jumbling Venn Diagram Data Interpretation and Sufficiency Conclusions, Decision Making Similarities, Differences Analytical Reasoning Classification Directions Statement – Arguments, Assumptions General Science: Physics, Chemistry, Life Sciences (10th standard CBSE syllabus). Key Topics: Mechanics Heat, Thermodynamics Electricity, Magnetism Optics Atomic Structure Chemical Reactions Organic Chemistry Human Body, Health Environment, Ecology General Awareness and Current Affairs: Science and Technology Sports Culture Personalities Economics Politics National and International Events 2. CBT-2 Syllabus CBT-2 includes two parts with advanced topics. Part A: Mathematics: Same as CBT-1 (higher difficulty). General Intelligence and Reasoning: Same as CBT-1 (increased complexity). Basic Science and Engineering: Engineering Drawing (Projections, Views, Instruments, Lines, Geometric Figures) Units, Measurements Mass, Weight, Density Work, Power, Energy Speed, Velocity Heat, Temperature Basic Electricity Levers, Simple Machines Occupational Safety, Health Environment Education IT Literacy General Awareness and Current Affairs: Same as CBT-1 (focus on recent developments). Part B (Trade-Specific): Relevant to ALP qualifications (ITI/Apprenticeship/Diploma). Trades: Fitter Electrician Instrument Mechanic Millwright/Maintenance Mechanic Mechanic (Radio & TV) Electronics Mechanic Mechanic (Motor Vehicle) Wireman Tractor Mechanic Armature & Coil Winder Mechanic (Diesel) Heat Engine Turner Machinist Refrigeration & Air-Conditioning Mechanic Engineering Disciplines: Mechanical Electrical Electronics Automobile Topics: Core concepts of the trade/discipline. Locomotive operations, maintenance. Safety protocols, tools, equipment. 3. CBAT Syllabus Purpose: Assess psychomotor and cognitive skills for safety-critical roles. Topics: Memory: Pattern/sequence recall. Concentration: Attention under time constraints. Perception: Speed, accuracy in visual stimuli. Reasoning: Logical decision-making. Motor Skills: Hand-eye coordination, reaction time.
